problem: Prior EQA methods either treat it as passive video QA without active exploration or restrict answers to a closed set of choices. White-box exploration methods such as Explore-EQA need VLM logits and cannot use black-box models like GPT-4o, and they lack an adaptive stopping rule.
motivation: Real robot assistants must explore unknown homes efficiently and answer open-ended questions without predefined options. Powerful VLMs are usually black boxes with no logit access. The paper observes that question-image relevancy from BLIP spikes on the frame that decides the answer, so it can serve as both a stopping signal and a retrieval criterion.
key_idea: Combine semantic-value-weighted frontier exploration guided by black-box VLM verbalized confidence with BLIP-relevancy outlier-based early stopping and top-K BLIP-retrieved RAG answering, so the agent explores, stops and answers open-vocabulary EQA efficiently.
insight: Adaptive stopping on a Z-score outlier of BLIP relevancy cuts steps: on HM-EQA, average steps are 30.16 versus 38.87 for Explore-EQA. Answering from the top-K relevant frames matters: K=5 gives 54.25 while K=1 gives 51.25 and K=10 gives 53.50, so too many frames distract the VLM. The stopping threshold trades accuracy against steps: Z=1 gives 47.75 and Z=3 gives 54.25. Black-box Explore-EQA with verbalized confidence (36.50) does worse than the logit version (39.00), so the gain comes mainly from the stopping and RAG modules and from using GPT-4o.
method: SFE: builds a semantic value map with frontier-based exploration (from Explore-EQA/Yamauchi); voxels seen in each RGB-D observation are marked explored and semantic values updated; candidate frontier directions are proposed to the VLM.

Verbalized Confidence (VC): prompts black-box GPT-4o for M=3 answers with confidences, normalizes them, groups semantically equivalent answers via the LLM, and picks the class with the highest cumulative confidence to update the semantic map.

Relevancy-based early stopping: computes BLIP-2 ITM similarity of each RGB frame with the question, fits a running mean and std over history, and stops when a frame's Z-score exceeds Z_th=3 (the answer-decisive frame); no stopping before step 10.
RAG answering: after stopping, retrieves the top K=5 history images by BLIP relevancy and feeds them to GPT-4o to generate a free-form answer without choices.
Open Explore EQA task: an open-vocabulary EQA task formulation with no answer choices and no prior scene knowledge; evaluated with LLM-Match (1-5 score mapped to 0-100) and average steps.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (gpt-4o-2024-05-13, frozen, black-box, T=1) + BLIP-2 ITM ViT-g (frozen)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D from a single front camera plus pose
setting.action_space: frontier-based waypoints/directions selected among candidate frontiers
setting.simulator: Habitat-Sim (HM3D scenes, HM-EQA dataset); real-world demos on Husky and UR5e
setting.privileged: scene dimensions (preliminary scene size) for map construction; otherwise none

results: On a 100-question HM-EQA subset with choices removed, EfficientEQA reaches 54.25 LLM-Match with 30.16 average steps. This beats Explore-EQA (39.00, 38.87 steps), black-box Explore-EQA (36.50) and the blind LLM (29.50). The abstract claims over 15% higher accuracy and over 20% fewer steps.
limitations: Evaluated on only 100 of the 500 HM-EQA questions, a small evaluation with no variance reported; the baseline comparison is against modified Explore-EQA, since no direct baselines exist.
The stopping rule depends on a hyperparameter Z_th and on the assumption that BLIP relevancy is roughly normal for non-decisive frames; no stopping before step 10.
The method assumes preliminary scene dimensions, does not involve object interaction, and relies on commercial GPT-4o with LLM-based scoring.
